basis: The county's heat curve must show a heat effect: median model RR (harm/harm_daily_{fips}.csv rr) on the county's hottest 1% of days (tmean_c >= its 99th percentile) is at least 1.01.

Heat deaths must be plausible: heat_attr_deaths_per_year (harm/harm_summary_{fips}.json) per 100k mean residents (data/processed/county_population_long.csv) is at least 1.0/yr, about a third of the published US benchmark of ~3.2/100k/yr (schema/response_benchmarks.csv B07, Weinberger et al. 2020).

calc:evidence:portfolio.formula: Σ_days deaths_day × (1 − Π_options (1 − min(1, segment_share × coverage × m) × effect × active)); cost = tier cost × m; at most one threshold per strategy; best mix = multi-start greedy + Pareto filter (pipeline/portfolio.py)

ev:EV04.finding: Pakistan RCT: no mortality effect but 38% fewer unscheduled hospital visits. India program: ~41% fewer heat-stroke deaths. China: ~20% less heat illness (not significant). Australia RCT: more protective behavior, less self-reported heat stress. Outdoor worker RCT: non-significant.
ev:EV04.source: Burke, Wilson et al. (2026), Understanding and addressing temperature impacts on mortality (reference numbers)

ev:EV09.finding: California standard: 87% reduction in hot-day injury effect and 33% fewer outdoor-worker heat deaths (neither significant). Dallas rest-break ordinance: no significant effect. El Salvador water/rest: better kidney function (imprecise).
ev:EV09.notes: Applies to worker population only, not whole-population burden.
ev:EV09.source: Burke, Wilson et al. (2026), Understanding and addressing temperature impacts on mortality (reference numbers)

ev:EV10.finding: No randomized or quasi-experimental evaluation of cooling centers on health identified.
ev:EV10.notes: Very common in plans; key 'popular but unproven' case.
ev:EV10.source: Burke, Wilson et al. (2026), Understanding and addressing temperature impacts on mortality (reference numbers)

ev:EV13.finding: US: doubling home-heating prices raised winter all-cause mortality ~2%. Japan: higher residential energy prices raised mortality on days below 0C. New Zealand: higher electricity prices raised asthma admissions. China subsidized heating: ~50% lower cold-related mortality. UK Winter Fuel Payment RD: no individual health effect (DiD result coded under income).
ev:EV13.notes: Paper: reducing heating cost reduces cold harm; LIHEAP evaluation is an open research need.
ev:EV13.source: Burke, Wilson et al. (2026), Understanding and addressing temperature impacts on mortality (reference numbers)

ev:EV17.finding: Japan post-Fukushima conservation push raised temperature mortality on hot and cold days; average savings target roughly doubled the mortality impact of a 30C day and raised a 0C day's impact ~10%.
ev:EV17.notes: Flag any plan that asks residents to conserve power during heat/cold.
ev:EV17.source: Burke, Wilson et al. (2026), Understanding and addressing temperature impacts on mortality (reference numbers)

ev:EV21.finding: New Zealand RCT: non-polluting heaters raised indoor temps and cut child asthma doctor visits ~30%.
ev:EV21.source: Burke, Wilson et al. (2026), Understanding and addressing temperature impacts on mortality (reference numbers)

ev:EV27.finding: Mexico coverage expansion: 36% smaller moderate-cold mortality effect. Colombia: ~55% smaller cold mortality effect.
ev:EV27.notes: No US study; transport with caution.
ev:EV27.source: Burke, Wilson et al. (2026), Understanding and addressing temperature impacts on mortality (reference numbers)
